youtube.title: Why America Outlawed the Streets on Its Own Postcards
youtube.description:
Most of the streets on American postcards could not legally be built in those towns today. In Manhattan, about 40% of buildings break current zoning. This wasn't an accident or a change in taste: a 1916 Berkeley realtor's single-family rule, the 1926 Supreme Court case Euclid v. Ambler, FHA mortgage rules from 1938, and parking minimums made the corner-store neighborhood illegal. Some cities are now undoing it. The Hidden Why: the real reason behind the things you see every day.

Sources: Euclid v. Ambler Realty (1926); FHA Underwriting Manual (1938); Shoup, The High Cost of Free Parking; NYT Upshot (2016, 2019).
